split.name_en: Criminal investigation and trial of a sitting prime minister or minister
split.plus_en: More protection from investigation and trial while in office (immunity, ban on investigating a sitting prime minister)
split.minus_en: A sitting prime minister or minister can be investigated and tried like anyone else
split.statement_en: Prosecutors should be able to investigate and try a sitting prime minister or minister, even if this disrupts the work of an elected government.

split.name_en: Indicted prime minister or minister staying in office
split.plus_en: A person under indictment may form a government or keep serving as prime minister or minister
split.minus_en: Indictment ends or bars service as prime minister or minister
split.statement_en: A person charged with a crime should not be allowed to serve as prime minister or minister, even before a court rules on guilt.

reason: Two distinct, well-known debates share this direction. Rows 1,3,6,10 (weight 30.8, ~63%, incl. the only bill with votes) are about immunity / banning investigation of a sitting prime minister — the current q64 text fits them exactly and stays unchanged. Rows 2,4,5,7,9 (weight 17, ~35%, initiators only) are about whether an indicted person must leave office or may form a government — a different question: a voter can support prosecuting a sitting prime minister yet oppose forced resignation before a verdict. Both parts keep agree = less of the direction. Row 8 (general Basic Law on integrity in government, weight 1) is too vague to assign from its title and is left out.
